The ~29 GB of safetensors are `mmap`ed from a bind mount, so every page read is charged to **the container's** cgroup as file cache; the cgroup pins itself against its own ceiling and cgroup reclaim swaps the container's *anonymous* pages -- the live working set, including the host staging buffers the card's copy engine reads through userptr mappings -- to make room for more file cache. This is the same error as the September 17 `MemoryMax=4G` "tripwire" on a runner with a ~25 GiB working set (row above): a cap under the working set thrashes in reclaim instead of tripping. **Fix: make `--memory-swap` equal `--memory`** (cgroup v2 `memory.swap.max=0`), so at the ceiling the kernel must drop clean, re-readable file pages instead of swapping live anonymous ones; anon is 6.91 GiB against the 12 GiB cap, ~5 GiB of headroom, `file_dirty 0`. **Do not edit `serve.py` first** -- both launchers are byte-pinned by published evidence packets. Validate on three service starts that were going to happen anyway with [`scripts/apply-container-noswap.sh`](../../scripts/apply-container-noswap.sh) (applies `docker update` to the new container ~60 s before the weight load; refuses if it finds the container already past 6 GiB), gating on container `pswpout` ~0, `memory.events oom_kill` 0, ready and strict 12/12; then edit both launchers, regenerate the packets and re-run `guides.yml` and acceptance. The one-card profiles carry the same cap plus 2.368 GiB of host-resident embedding table (`B70_CPU_EMBED=1`) and swapped 2.2-2.7 GiB per start on 2026-09-17, so they need their own `memory.stat anon` read before inheriting the change. **Not proven:** that any of this causes the copy-engine faults -- this start swapped 4.4 GiB and did not fault. One correction came out of it: **`anon` is 8.95 GiB, not 6.91** -- the earlier reading was taken while 2-3 GiB of the container's anonymous memory sat in swap and was therefore uncounted, so headroom under the 12 GiB cap is ~3 GiB, not ~5, and the one-card estimate becomes 8.3-8.8 GiB anon with 3.2-3.7 GiB of headroom.
